query: Why do some travel expenses get declined, and which factors contribute the most?

per_column.name: is_travel_related
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant to a travel-focused query as a grouping axis. Grounding is only moderate: none of the sampled rows are travel items, so the flag's derivation for the 'true' rows cannot be verified from provided evidence, though the 'false' assignments on asset rows are sound.

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: Categorises the ci/description into asset types, a reasonable new grouping axis. Values map cleanly onto the source text (hardware_device, cloud_service correctly read). Somewhat tangential to travel declines but usable for segmenting expense types.

per_column.name: expense_entry_origin
per_column.rationale: Origin (automated vs manual) is a plausible driver of declines. But distinctions like 'explicit_purchase' vs 'manual_procurement' vs 'new_acquisition' on near-identical descriptions ('Addition of new hardware asset' -> explicit_purchase; 'Procurement of new hardware asset' -> manual_procurement) appear under-warranted by the text, indicating some fabricated granularity.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: Trivially derived from presence of the existing source_id column, so it is largely redundant restatement with low analytical leverage, though perfectly grounded and could weakly flag data-provenance differences.

per_column.name: processing_lag_category
per_column.rationale: Processing delay is a strong candidate factor for declines and a genuinely useful binned axis derived from opened_at/processed_date. Grounding good, though the 'long_delay_over_7_days' labels cannot be fully checked without opened_at in samples; nan correctly maps to not_processed.

per_column.name: department_group
per_column.rationale: Department is a reasonable factor to compare decline rates against, but it largely duplicates the existing department column (normalisation only), limiting new leverage. Values not shown in samples so grounding is inferred; NULL handling is acceptable.

per_column.name: asset_action_type
per_column.rationale: Highly correlated with asset_category and expense_entry_origin (new_acquisition tracks hardware/procurement), so it is largely a restatement adding little independent axis. Grounding is moderate; distinctions rest on subtle wording.

judge.rationale: The columns provide several usable grouping axes for a decline analysis (processing lag, department, travel flag, asset category), and most values are sound readings of the asset-oriented source text. However, the set skews toward IT-asset provenance rather than travel-specific decline drivers, and there is redundancy among expense_entry_origin, asset_category, and asset_action_type. Some fine-grained origin/action labels assert distinctions not clearly supported by near-identical source descriptions, indicating localized hallucination. Overall moderately useful and mostly grounded.
